annotations.text:
D · Workbench — Graphite, Libre Franklin + JetBrains Mono
The strip stays 460 wide. The SolidWorks section in it is now a two-line bar: what Export will do next, the insert checkbox, and a Curves button. Pressing it docks a 360-wide flyout to the right of the window, full height, so a long list of ribs gets the whole column rather than a five-row box at the bottom. Hide collapses it back; on an ultrawide the window simply grows sideways.
The flyout holds the part, where its settings are kept, Refresh / New curve, the curve tree, and a card for the selected record with its settings in one line.

D · Pick feedback — the three states of Pick from SolidWorks
The branch shows one sentence and four buttons, so a successful plane click looks the same as nothing. Here every step has its own row: a tick and what was read, a ring for the step awaiting a click (a refusal shows in red on that row), a hollow ring for what is still to come. Skip sits on the optional step; Cancel and Use what I picked stay in the corners.
Afterwards the picked values are tinted and tagged, and the header readout says where the plane came from.

Settled: option 4, Libre Franklin + JetBrains Mono, was chosen. D · Font options — six professional pairings, in Graphite
Each cell is the same set of controls; only the type changes, and the mono face for numbers changes with it. Sizes are nudged half a pixel where a face runs small or wide, so the comparison is fair.
1 IBM Plex is corporate engineering. 2 Source Sans is the neutral compact one. 3 Fira is the sturdier developer-tool feel. 4 Libre Franklin has the industrial drawing-sheet heritage. 5 Red Hat is modern enterprise. 6 Noto is the plain workhorse.
Not shown: Segoe UI, the Windows system face — it needs no download and is what the current tkinter app already uses; on this canvas it would render as your Mac's system font, so it is not a fair sample here.

Settled: Graphite was chosen. D · Accent options — four starting points, most colour to least
The same controls in each: checkboxes, the pick tracker's active step, the primary button. Everything else stays white and grey; the state greens and reds are unchanged.
1 Windows blue is the OS accent and looks native. 2 Navy is still blue but dark and conservative. 3 Steel is a grey with a hint of blue. 4 Graphite drops the accent entirely — black controls, colour only for state.
Corner radius differs too (4 · 2 · 3 · 2 px), as a second lever to carry forward.

A · Property sheet
Every field on screen at once, no scrolling, native Windows look. Reads like a CAD property manager, so it sits comfortably next to SolidWorks.
Trade-off: dense. The long hints become tooltips, so a first-time user gets less hand-holding.
Drawn before the solidworks-link branch; D carries the new panel and pick controls.

B · Guided steps
One stage open at a time; finished stages collapse to a one-line summary you can re-open. Hides fields that don't apply (P1–P3 on a main plane).
Trade-off: more clicks, and the whole state is never visible at once. Power users will want A or D.
Drawn before the solidworks-link branch; D carries the new panel and pick controls.
